title: ByteMe CTF 26
description:
ByteMe CTF 26 is a hybrid Jeopardy-style Capture The Flag competition organized by OWASP PCCOE and the Department of Computer Engineering, PCCOE, Pune.

The event is designed for college students and provides hands-on exposure to practical cybersecurity through challenges across multiple domains, including OSINT, Web Security, Cryptography, Digital Forensics, Steganography, Reverse Engineering, Binary Exploitation, AI Security, and Miscellaneous.

The competition will be conducted in both online and onsite modes, with participants solving challenges and submitting flags through the CTF platform. Challenges will range from beginner-friendly to advanced difficulty levels. Both online and onsite participants will compete through the same CTF platform, with separate event instances used for each mode.

Date: 9 October 2026
Time: 09:00 AM – 06:00 PM IST
Mode: Online + Onsite
Venue: PCCOE, Pune
Format: Jeopardy
Platform: CTF7
Team Size: 1–2 Members
Eligibility: College Students
Website: https://bytemectf.owasppccoe.in/

Online Registration: https://ctf7.com/console/events/byteme-ctf/
Onsite Registration: https://unstop.com/p/byteme-ctf-26-pimpri-chinchwad-college-of-engineering-1760412
Discord: https://discord.com/invite/9BpjC2TxeK

prize.description:
Total Prize Pool Worth ₹1,50,000+

Online — Global
Top 5 teams — Cybersecurity Certification Vouchers

Onsite — PCCOE
Cash Prizes + Cybersecurity Certification Vouchers + Goodies

Cash prizes are applicable to the Onsite category.

title: Hacker's Gambit 2026 (Round 2 – Grand Finale)
description:
The Grand Finale is the final stage of Hackers Gambit 2026, where the Top 15 teams selected from the Online Qualifier will compete for the championship title. This 24-hour, on-site Capture The Flag (CTF) competition is designed to simulate real-world cybersecurity scenarios and evaluate participants' ability to solve complex security challenges under pressure.

Hosted at Jaihind College of Engineering, Kuran, the Grand Finale brings together the highest-performing teams for an intensive competition featuring advanced challenges across multiple cybersecurity domains. Participants will demonstrate their technical expertise, analytical thinking, teamwork, strategic decision-making, and adaptability while competing against some of the best cybersecurity talent.

Challenges may cover domains including:

Web Security
Cryptography
Reverse Engineering
Digital Forensics
Binary Exploitation (Pwn)
Open Source Intelligence (OSINT)
Steganography
Network Security
Miscellaneous Challenges

Throughout the competition, teams will work continuously for 24 hours, solving progressively challenging problems to accumulate points on the official scoreboard. The competition will conclude with score verification by the organizing committee, followed by the official announcement of winners during the Awards & Closing Ceremony.

The Grand Finale provides participants with an opportunity to showcase their cybersecurity skills in a highly competitive environment while networking with industry professionals, sponsors, security researchers, and fellow cybersecurity enthusiasts.

Key Highlights
Mode: Offline
Venue: Jaihind College of Engineering, Kuran, Maharashtra, India
Duration: 24 Hours
Format: Advanced Jeopardy-style Capture The Flag (CTF)
Eligibility: Top 15 teams qualified from the Online Qualifier
Challenge Categories: Web Security, Cryptography, Reverse Engineering, Digital Forensics, Binary Exploitation (Pwn), OSINT, Steganography, Network Security, and Miscellaneous
Scoring: Points awarded based on successful flag submissions and challenge completion
Winner Selection: Final rankings are determined based on the official scoreboard and verification by the organizing committee.
Awards: Winners will receive cash prizes, trophies, certificates, sponsor rewards, and the title of Hackers Gambit 2026 Champion.

description:

Challenges cover web, pwn, crypto, reverse engineering, forensics, misc, Linux, Windows, and operational security, with scenarios connected to energy, telecom, healthcare, finance, and defense environments.

The competition is somewhat beginner-friendly but realism-driven.

title: SpookyCTF 2026
description:
EVENT TIME HAS BEEN SHIFTED TO START AND END 4 HOURS AFTER TIME LISTED ABOVE

REGISTRATION IS NOW AVAILABLE!

BOO!!

Welcome to SpookyCTF 2026! Organized by the New Jersey Institute of Technology's Cyber Security Network (formerly known as NICC), this is our annual Halloween CTF event, open to all!

We've made this CTF beginner-friendly, with a mix of harder challenges. Our mission is to help beginners develop professionally in cybersecurity while still keeping things fun! You'll be pushed to stay curious and strengthen your reasoning skills across challenges of varying difficulty.

Our challenge categories include Binary Exploitation/Reverse Engineering, Cryptography, Forensics, OSINT, Web, and Misc. Expect weird but fun challenges developed by our team at CSN.

SpookyCTF is hybrid — in person at NJIT and open to virtual attendees!

Join our Discord to tap in: https://discord.gg/NeHyp5fFHW

AI assistance is allowed but discouraged. Learning is part of the challenge — use your brain!
Automated AI agents for solving challenges are strictly forbidden. Any detected automated AI usage will result in disqualification.

title: BlackAlps CTF 2026
description:
The BlackAlps CTF will be held at the end of the BlackAlps conference in Yverdon-les-Bains in Switzerland. It's a CTF for all level including from beginner up to advanced team.

The CTF will last 5 hours and be on site for about 300 people.

There is no specific categories.

Registration is mandatory.

Welcome at 18:45. Start at 19:00. End at 23:30. Awards ceremony at 23:45.

prize.description:
We observe that the arrival of artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly affected the spirit of CTFs.
To keep the event engaging, the #BlackAlps26 CTF is introducing a new format that reflects what CTFs mean to us: having fun, learning and sharing.

For this year we are introducing Write-up presentations: participants will be able to present their solutions on stage during the final hour and prizes will be awarded to write-up presenters.

title: Mimic
description: Mimic is an online Jeopardy-style CTF by Rare Byte Hub. Some challenges are exactly what they look like, and some aren't. Figure out which is which. There's something for everyone, from beginners to experienced players. Teams of 1-4 members.

title: CSAW CTF Final Round 2026
description: CSAW CTF is one of the oldest and biggest CTFs. Designed as an entry-level, jeopardy-style CTF, this competition is for students who are trying to break into the field of security, as well as for advanced students and industry professionals who want to practice their skills.

title: Platypwn 2026
description:
The Platypwn 2026 is an online Jeopardy CTF which offers easy challenges for beginners, but also medium and difficult challenges for advanced players.

See https://platypwnies.de/events/platypwn for further details.

title: WolvCTF 2026
description:
Our challenges range from beginner to hard in difficulty. Our esteemed members have worked tirelessly to bring new and stimulating CTF challenges to pose varying levels of difficulty and topic (RE, binary exploit, web exploit, cryptography, forensics, osint, misc.). 

There are two divisions, Open and University of Michigan students. No team limit sizes.

Sponsors to be announced!

title: InIt CTF
description:
InIt CTF is HII's (Hackers in India) beginner-focused Capture The Flag event, free and open to participants across India and internationally. 8 hours, Jeopardy-style, solo or teams of up to 4, across Web, Crypto, Forensics, OSINT, and Misc — mostly easy/medium with a couple of harder challenges for experienced players. This edition is sponsored by .xyz, who are providing free domain codes for participants, with additional sponsors being confirmed. Register at

hackersinindia.com/init-ctf.

prize.description: Finalized with sponsors — includes .xyz domain codes and vouchers/prizes from additional sponsors, confirmed closer to the event. All participants receive a certificate.

title: EyesOpenCTF 7th edition
description:
EyesOpenCTF 2026 is a FREE CTF competition organized as part of the 7th edition of EOCON.

This year, the competition goes far beyond a traditional CTF.
You are not simply joining to solve isolated challenges. You are entering The Convergence, a live 48-hour cyber adventure in which reality itself is beginning to fracture.
Across more than 40 challenges and 8 disciplines, teams will investigate corrupted systems, recover hidden Reality Fragments, unlock classified dossiers, expose compromised actors, and gradually reconstruct the truth behind a phenomenon threatening the entire world.

Every flag matters.
Each solved challenge can reveal new intelligence, unlock characters and locations, alter the mission briefing, and move the story forward in real time. The competition platform becomes a living investigation that evolves with the progress of the Operators.

Expect  : 
- web exploitation, 
- digital forensics, 
- reverse engineering, 
- binary exploitation, 
- cryptography, 
- OSINT, 
- AI security, and more—woven into a single coherent mission unlike any previous EyesOpenCTF.

Built for teams from around the world and open to different experience levels, EyesOpenCTF is both a proving ground and an immersive narrative experience where competitors can learn, compete, get noticed, and join a fast-growing international cybersecurity community.

As part of EOCON, the competition also connects participants with experts, researchers, recruiters, entrepreneurs, and emerging talent from Africa and beyond. It is a place where technical ability meets storytelling, where discoveries change the mission, and where tomorrow’s collaborations, careers, and opportunities begin.

Form your team. Enter the Protocol. Recover the Fragments.

Register: https://eyesopensecurity.com/ctf-briefing.html

Direct Form: https://eyesopensecurity.com/?modal=ctf

SPONSORS :
- CyberDefenders (https://cyberdefenders.org)
- JetBrains (https://jetbrains.com)
- Netticket (https://netticket.net)
- ExamBoot (https://examboot.net)

1st: 300 USD + 1 year ExamBoot subscription. (500 USD dedicated for the 1st Cameroonian local on the scoreboard) 
3-month BlueYard Pro subscription, 1 Free annual personal subscriptions to a chosen JetBrains IDE.

2nd: 1 year ExamBoot subscription. 2-month BlueYard Pro subscription. 1 Free annual personal subscriptions to a chosen JetBrains IDE.

3rd: 6 month ExamBoot subscription. 1 Free annual personal subscriptions to a chosen JetBrains IDE.

title: Outback Overflow
description:
Outback Overflow is a free online jeopardy-style CTF built for high schoolers across Australia. Run by the High School Cybersecurity Community, it's designed to be a stepping stone for students getting into cyber security, whether you've never touched a terminal or you're already popping shells.

Our goal is simple: grow the number of young people in cyber security and give Australian high schoolers a CTF they can call their own.

Sponsors: TBD (if you would like to sponsor please reach out to contact@hscyber.org or join our discord!)

Join our discord to talk to other players!
https://discord.gg/xWPndqMCfA

title: Crate-CTF 2026
description:
Crate-CTF is an annual Capture The Flag (CTF) competition organised by the Swedish Defence Research Agency in collaboration with the Swedish Armed Forces, designed to introduce high school and university students to the field of cybersecurity. This year we return for our seventh CTF, with challenges for all skill levels from beginners to seasoned CTF players. The challenges are categorised into web exploitation, reverse engineering, binary exploitation, cryptography, forensics, OSINT, networking and the all-encompassing "other".

While the event will be conducted in Swedish, international participants are also welcome to join (using translation tools as needed). Communication with challenge authors and administrators can be conducted in English.

title: CyberSci Regional Qualifiers 2026-27
description:
CyberSci is Canada's national Cyber Security Challenge for university and college students.
- Think you've got an elite team of students? Come and prove it. Our winners will go on to compete against the best in the world.
- Just starting out? This is the best way to learn and rise to the top.
- Annual in-person events since 2016. (Online during Covid.) Over 500 students so far.

Format:
- Modified jeopardy style. Realistic IT environment.
- Regional qualifiers are held in Nov-Dec each year.
- National finals are the following July.
- Winning teams represent Canada at international events in the Fall.

For Regionals (qualifiers):
We do hacking in the morning, interviews in the afternoon, and job offers by supper (for intern/summer/coop jobs).
- Full-time job offers take a few more days.
- Students register their team through their school instructor or computer club. Max 2 teams per school.

For nationals:
Participants will be the winning team from each regional/qualifier
- PLUS one all-juniors (19 and under)
- AND one all-women team (chosen from participants at the Regionals).
Two-day event.

prize.description:
Winners at Regionals get instant interviews and sometimes same-day job offers.

Winners at Nationals will represent Canada at international events in the Fall.

title: BlackHat MEA CTF Final 2026
description:
Black Hat MEA Capture The Flag (CTF) 2026 ?

The Black Hat MEA Capture The Flag (CTF) is the largest cybersecurity competition in the region and officially the largest Capture The Flag competition in the world, recognized with a Guinness World Record. Organized by the Saudi Federation for Cybersecurity, Programming and Drones (SAFCSP) in collaboration with Black Hat MEA, the competition brings together thousands of cybersecurity professionals, researchers, students, and enthusiasts from around the globe.

Powered by the FlagYard platform, the competition follows a Jeopardy-style format, where teams of 3–5 players compete across a range of cybersecurity challenges, including Web Exploitation, PWN, Digital Forensics, Reverse Engineering, Cryptography, and AI Hacking.

Competition Timeline

Registration: June 3 – August 29, 2026

Online Qualifiers: August 29, 2026 | 10:00 AM KSA (GMT+3) | Online

Thousands of participants will compete globally in teams of 3–5 members, with the top 150 teams qualifying for the final stage.

On-site Finals

The top 150 teams will be invited to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia for a 3-day final competition during Black Hat MEA, taking place from December 1–3, 2026.

Register Now:
https://flagyard.com/events/3468f495-a92c-498b-90c2-994dfb99ea0b

Support: blackhatctf@safcsp.org.sa

title: JerseyCTF VII
description:
Locations:

- In-Person @ NJIT Campus Center Ballroom, Newark, New Jersey

JerseyCTF is a beginner-friendly Capture the Flag competition that aims to inspire interest in cybersecurity. This competition is hosted by the NJIT Information & Cybersecurity Club, the NJIT Chapter of ACM, and the NJIT SCI program.

It is geared towards students, beginners, and professionals alike. JerseyCTF provides participants with jeopardy-style questions in categories including cryptography, forensics, binary exploitation/reversing, open-source intelligence, and web exploitation.

This CTF is held hybrid - with attendance virtually or in-person on NJIT's campus in Newark, New Jersey, USA.
